title: The mind is a machine that makes up stories
kicker: Why a sad day turns into a sad story
blurb: The mind turns what happens into stories about you and the world. Seeing them as stories makes room for other, more accurate ones.
description: A short talk on how the mind makes sense of the world by telling stories. Those stories are not always accurate, and a bad day can easily become a story about who you are. Once you see the pattern, you can ask what is really going on and choose a more flexible story.
takeaways: Everything you experience passes through the unconscious mind and then through personal models, such as models for language and for how you perceive sound.
The mind works to make sense of things, and a story that makes sense can win out over one that is accurate.
A bad day can turn into a story about yourself or the world, such as that you are a failure or that nothing works.
A more accurate story is often practical, for example that you feel sad because you skipped exercise or have not seen friends.
You will not stop making stories, but you can hold them more loosely and ask what you can do instead.
